This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P. (MV) No.1206/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Muvattupuzha, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 11/06/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 10/06/2015 at about 11:30 a.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL-44/B-8208 through the Muvattupuzha-Kothamangalam road and when he reached the place by name Kuroor Kara, Kothamangalam, KSRTC bus 2025:KER:40243 bearing registration no.KL-15-A-701 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 20,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The respondents filed a joint written statement denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver.

The injuries sustained, age, occupation and monthly income of the claim Ananthu Suresh vs Managing Director on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148050070/

sentences.text: It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
4. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A15 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.
Ext.C1 is the Report issued by the Medical Board, Medical College Hospital, Kottayam.

sentences.text:
5. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an 2025:KER:40243 amount of 17,04,200/- together with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
6.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
7. Heard both sides 8.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
In the petition it is alleged that the claim petitioner, an Accountant, aged 21 years at the time of the incident, was earning of 15,000/- per month.

In support of the claim, Ext.A10 certificate dated 05/05/2017 issued by Civil Engineer, Anil Homes,
Building Construction and Design was produced.
Marking of the document was objected to.
The claim petitioner did not examine the person who issued Ext.A10 and hence as the 2025:KER:40243 contents was not proved, the Tribunal did not rely on the same.
In the absence of evidence, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 7,000/- which is stated to be on the lower side.
As noticed earlier, in the claim petition the specific allegation is that the claim petitioner was working as an Accountant at the time of the incident.
However, as per Ext.A10 dated 05/05/2017 he is stated to be a Supervisor.
The claim petitioner when examined as PW1 has a case that he was working as Accountant and Supervisor of Anil Homes, Kothamangalam.
He was a part time student of ACCA and that he had goat-farming too and thus his income was 15,000/- per month.
As the contents of Ext.A10 has not been proved, the Tribunal was right in not relying on the same and fixing the notional income.
There is no evidence to support his other claims.
Hence, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, the notional income can be fixed as 10,000/-.

sentences.text: Loss of earnings An amount of 1,80,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 56,000/-.

As per materials before the Court, the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner are:-
"(1) Crush degloving injury Lt. Leg from knee to ankle. (2) Type III B compound dislocaiton ankle Lt. (3) Comminuted fracture calcaneum (4) Heel pad avulsion (5)
lacerated wound Lt. Knee."

sentences.text: 3 It is brought to my notice that the claim petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 73 days and that he had to undergo 9 surgeries.
Hence, in these circumstances, I find that in all probability the claim petitioner must have been unable to work for a period of atleast one year.
Therefore, towards loss of earnings the amount will be 10,000/- x 12 months = 1,20,000/-.
Bystander expenses
An amount of 30,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 18,250/-.
The claim petitioner as noticed earlier was hospitalized for a period of 73 days and had to undergo 9 surgeries.
In the light of the period of hospitalization 2025:KER:40243 and the number of medical interventions he had to undergo, I find that bystander expenses of 30,000/- as claimed can be granted.
Pain and sufferings
An amount of 1,25,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 75,000/-.
In the light of the injuries, the hospitalization and the number of surgeries undergone, I find that an amount of 85,000/- would be just and reasonable.
Permanent disability
An amount of 8,00,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 7,86,240/-.

According to the learned counsel for the claim petitioner in the light of Ext.C1 certificate of the Medical Board, the claim petitioner has sustained total disability of 52% and therefore, going by the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi, 2017 (5) KHC 350 : (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Tribunal while assessing compensation under this head ought to have granted additions to the established income which has not been done in this case.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi, 2017 (5) KHC 350 : (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case the claim petitioner was a 21 year old boy who as per Ext.C1 has sustained 49% disability with respect to his left lower limb.
Therefore, I find that addition of 40% to the established income while computing compensation under this head can be granted.
